source_text: Ὁ οὖν Κάϊν καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσχεν υἱόν, ᾧ ὄνομα Ἐνώχ. Καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πόλιν, ἣν ἐπωνόμασεν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἐνώχ. Ἀπὸ τότε ἀρχὴ ἐγένετο τοῦ οἰκοδομεῖσθαι πόλεις, καὶ τοῦτο πρὸ κατακλυσμοῦ· οὐχ ὡς Ὅμηρος ψεύδεται λέγων· Οὐ γάρ πω πεπόλιστο πόλις μερόπων ἀνθρώπων. Τῷ δὲ Ἐνὼχ ἐγενήθη υἱὸς ὀνόματι Γαϊδάδ· ἐγέννησεν τὸν καλούμενον Μεήλ, καὶ Μεὴλ τὸν Μαθουσάλα, καὶ Μαθουσάλα τὸν Λάμεχ. Ὁ δὲ Λάμεχ ἔλαβεν ἑαυτῷ δύο γυναῖκας, αἷς ὀνόματα Ἀδᾶ καὶ Σελᾶ. Ἔκτοτε ἀρχὴ ἐγένετο τῆς πολυμιξίας, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς μουσικῆς. Τῷ γὰρ Λάμεχ ἐγένοντο τρεῖς υἱοί, Ὠβὴλ Ἰουβὰλ Θοβέλ. Καὶ ὁ μὲν Ὠβὴλ ἐγένετο ἀνὴρ ἐν σκηναῖς κτηνοτροφῶν, Ἰουβὰλ δέ ἐστιν ὁ καταδείξας ψαλτήριον καὶ κιθάραν, Θοβὲλ δὲ ἐγένετο σφυροκόπος χαλκεὺς χαλκοῦ καὶ σιδήρου. Ἕως μὲν οὖν τούτου ἔσχεν τὸν κατάλογον τὸ σπέρμα τοῦ Κάϊν· καὶ τὸ λοιπὸν εἰς λήθην αὐτοῦ γέγονεν τὸ σπέρμα τῆς γενεαλογίας, διὰ τὸ ἀδελφοκτονῆσαι αὐτὸν τὸν ἀδελφόν. Εἰς τὸν τόπον δὲ τοῦ Ἄβελ ἔδωκεν ὁ θεὸς συλλαβεῖν τὴν Εὔαν καὶ τεκεῖν υἱὸν, ὃς κέκληται Σήθ· ἀφ᾿ οὗ τὸ λοιπὸν γένος τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὁδεύει μέχρι τοῦ δεῦρο. Τοῖς δὲ βουλομένοις καὶ φιλομαθέσιν καὶ περὶ πασῶν τῶν γενεῶν εὔκολόν ἐστιν ἐπιδεῖξαι διὰ τῶν ἁγίων γραφῶν. Καὶ γὰρ ἐκ μέρους ἡμῖν γεγένηται ἤδη λόγος ἐν ἑτέρῳ λόγῳ, ὡς ἐπάνω προειρήκαμεν, τῆς γενεαλογίας ἡ τάξις ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ βίβλῳ τῇ περὶ ἱστοριῶν. Ταῦτα δὲ πάντα ἡμᾶς διδάσκει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, τὸ διὰ Μωσέως καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν προφητῶν, ὥστε τὰ καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς τοὺς θεοσεβεῖς ἀρχαιότερα γράμματα τυγχάνει, οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀληθέστερα πάντων συγγραφέων καὶ ποιητῶν δείκνυται ὄντα.Ἀλλὰ μὴν καὶ τὰ περὶ τῆς μουσικῆς ἐφλυάρησάν τινες εὑρετὴν Ἀπόλλωνα γεγενῆσθαι· ἄλλοι δὲ Ὄρφεα ἀπὸ τῆς τῶν ὀρνέων ἡδυφωνίας φασὶν ἐξευρηκέναι τὴν μουσικήν. Κενὸς δὲ καὶ μάταιος ὁ λόγος αὐτῶν δείκνυται· μετὰ γὰρ πολλὰ ἔτη τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ οὗτοι ἐγένοντο. Τὰ δὲ περὶ τοῦ Νῶε, ὅς κέκληται ὑπὸ ἐνίων Δευκαλίων, ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ ᾗ προειρήκαμεν ἡ διήγησις ἡμῖν γεγένηται· ᾗ, εἰ βούλει, καὶ σὺ δύνασαι ἐντυχεῖν.
pass_a_gloss: So Cain also had a son, whose name was Enoch. And he built a city, which he named after his son Enoch. From that time on, the building of cities began, and this was before the flood; not as Homer falsely says: 'For not yet had a city been built for mortal men.' And to Enoch was born a son named Gaidad; he fathered the one called Meel, and Meel fathered Mathusala, and Mathusala fathered Lamech. And Lamech took for himself two wives, whose names were Ada and Sella. From that time on, the beginning of bigamy and also of music came about. For to Lamech were born three sons, Obel, Jubal, and Tubel. And Obel became a man who lived in tents and raised livestock, Jubal was the one who showed the psaltery and the harp, and Tubel became a hammerer of copper and iron. So far, then, the seed of Cain had the catalog; and from then on, the seed of his genealogy fell into oblivion because he had murdered his brother. But in the place of Abel, God gave Eve to conceive and bear a son, who was called Seth; from whom the rest of the human race proceeds until now. For those who wish and love to learn, it is easy to show through the holy scriptures about all the generations. For already a partial account has been given to us in another account, as we said above, the order of the genealogy in the first book about histories. The Holy Spirit teaches us all these things through Moses and the rest of the prophets, so that the writings that are sacred to us are found to be more ancient and also more true than all other writers and poets. But some have foolishly talked about the inventor of music, saying that Apollo was the inventor; others say that Orpheus discovered music from the sweet sound of birds. But their talk is empty and vain; for these men lived many years after the flood. The account about Noah, who is also called Deucalion by some, has been given in the book we mentioned earlier; which, if you wish, you also can examine.
pass_b_english: Cain also fathered a son named Enoch, and he built a city which he named after his son Enoch (Genesis 4:17). From that point onward the building of cities began, and this occurred before the flood; not as Homer falsely says, 'For not yet had a city been built for mortal men.'

To Enoch was born a son named Gaidad; Gaidad fathered Meel, Meel fathered Mathusala, and Mathusala fathered Lamech. Lamech took two wives, Ada and Sella, and from that time the practice of bigamy and the origin of music began. Lamech had three sons: Obel, Jubal, and Tubel. Obel became a man who lived in tents and raised livestock; Jubal was the one who introduced the psaltery and the harp; and Tubel became a metalworker, forging copper and iron.

Thus the line of Cain had a recorded catalog up to this point, but afterward his genealogy fell into oblivion because he had murdered his brother. In place of Abel, God gave Eve to conceive and bear a son named Seth, from whom the rest of humanity descends to this day. For anyone who wishes and loves to learn, it is easy to demonstrate every generation through the holy scriptures. A partial account has already been given in another work, as we noted above, outlining the genealogy in the first book of histories. The Holy Spirit teaches us all these things through Moses and the other prophets, so that our sacred writings are shown to be more ancient and also more true than those of any other writers and poets.

Some have foolishly claimed that Apollo invented music, while others say Orpheus discovered it from the sweet song of birds. Their claims are empty and vain, for these figures lived many years after the flood.
The account of Noah, who is also called Deucalion by some, has been presented in the book mentioned earlier; if you wish, you may examine it as well.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Greek text. Pass A provides a complete literal translation, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that preserves all nuances, including the distinction between the 'catalog' and the 'oblivion' of the genealogy. Scripture citations (Genesis 4:17) are correctly added to the English text to identify the allusion. The title 'Cain's Descendants' accurately names the thought of the chapter.
